comment: Lectures are informative but get sidetracked often, and sometimes we do a lot of Excel files that aren't super helpful. Not too many assignments, just weekly homework and quizzes. Tests are pretty difficult, but he is very understanding and willing to help. Also, very willing to explain concepts people don't understand individually in office hours.

Dr. Hamilton is a funny and caring guy who wants his students to understand statistics. However he sometimes forgets that he has a doctorate in this field and his students are undergraduates taking their first statistics class. Be prepared to not know what you are doing on any of the units until right before the test, as he is hesitant to explain.

Hamilton is fine if you need the credit. He's not engaging and the content covered is mundane at best. The quizzes given every week are nothing like the test and he is relatively difficult to access outside of class. Besides that, a pretty easy course.
His lectures are difficult to follow and unorganized, and he doesn't answer questions that are asked. The tests aren't similar to the practice problems and often go beyond what he taught in class.

Good and accommodating professor who wants us to learn. The textbook isn't that necessary, but make sure to pay attention to the lecture. ~5 Graded hw and Excel assignments, but they aren't terrible. He provides lots of practice where you should review what you learned in class. Weekly quiz based on class and a group take-home question to present.

Prof H. is a nice guy who just wants you to learn stats. 2 midterms, final, and a weekly quiz (quizzes were one question). Do the practice problems and you'll be fine for the exams. The Excel assignments will make you cry though.

Dr. Hamilton was great. The course only comes from lecture.  The course uses R which can be frustrating if you have never coded before, but is generally straight-forward. If you pay attention and stay ahead of assignments, you will succeed! Only con was that you don't know your grade at all throughout the course.
Great teacher who explains concepts very clearly.

His bstats class was poorly taught. He expects you to understand everything immediately because its "easy" (easy for him since he's done it for the past 20 years). He will get annoyed if you ask too many questions in office hours. Test does not match homework or resources given.

Accommodating person but not my favorite style professor. Weekly quizzes but I never knew what to study for them. Have no idea of my grade going into the final which made it extremely stressful. Excel homework but no clear guidance before hand. Wish had review sessions or gave clearer guidelines as to what was going to be on test.

I honestly like Professor Hamilton as a person, but I am not a fan of him as a professor. Especially for tests, he assigns practice problems that have minimal correlation to what is actually on the exam. However, he is very passionate about the subject and seems to still bump up students' grades a little.

prof hamilton's bstats class is very lecture heavy and most of his classes are him just talking at you while you take notes. Doesn't respond to emails, doesn't update grade book, confusing blackboard, doesnt teach what is on homework and exams. expects everyone to understand right away and gives hard tests. wouldn't take again. hard excel

I really liked Dr Hamilton as a person, but not so much as a professor. His lectures and grading criteria were confusing. His tests expected you to apply what you learned which was hard when there wasn't a firm grasp on the material in the first place. I think students succeed if they'd taken AP Stats, but everyone else struggled.

Professor H. is great at what he does. Friendly, accessible, humorous, knowledgeable. He gives partial credit and he wants his students to succeed. Low amount of hw, some coding modules. Two exams that can have a couple of tricky questions. You are also introduced to R, which is good. Clear instructions and grading. Highly recommended for ECON270!
One of the best professors at UR. Hes extremely dedicated and takes the trouble to make sure you understand the concepts. Very accessible outside of class for office hours
Very smart, impressive professor. His teaching always gives something you can't find in the textbook. Very likable. Makes class not boring. One of the best profs in the econ department.

Hamilton makes a highly difficult class interesting and engaging. That being said, it is very hard to get an A in the class. Tests are very challenging and draw from class notes, the book, and intuition. The R assignments are impossible, but he gives partial credit. If you want to do well, you will have to work for it and really learn Econometrics.
Professor Hamilton is the best.... he not only is a clear lecturer with fair homework & tests but he also has a great personality! I learned a lot while being challenged but not struggling.
He actually succeeds in making econometrics interesting. Hamilton  Schmidt. But his tests and homework can be very vague about what he's looking for,  but he grades easy, so it all balances out.

Hamilton is the man. Everybody raves about Nicholson but Hamilton actually teaches you. Always there for extra help if you need it. Explains complex topics with clarity and can answer just about any question you throw at him. Online HW is kind of annoying but not hard. Tests are tough but you can get an A in his class if you put in decent work.
I love professor Hamilton for B. stats. He is super interesting and knows a lot about statistics. He makes class fun and explains things very clearly. Definitely recommend.

Professor is a really nice guy. He relates well to the students and does a great job at making a boring subject somewhat interesting. Limited homework which it nice. Take good notes in class and study them well for the exams and you will be fine!

Such a cool guy. Loved his class. Not the easiest but he is willing to answer questions in and outside of class. Tries to make a boring subject sortof interesting. Doesn't give too much homework and tests and quizzes are fair.
I wish I could trace the probability density function of his chops.

I liked Hamilton. He’s got realistic expectations of what to expect from students and does a great job making a dry, boring class somewhat interesting with practical examples in daily coursework. The workload was reasonable. In my view, he’s the best runner-up to Nicholson for a Stats class. Recommended.
New professor. Not the best at instructing. But easy test
